record.title: China's transport ministry sets out 22 AI application scenarios for water transport
record.summary: China's Ministry of Transport issued a Chinese-language guide identifying 22 priority AI application scenarios for water transport, grouped under safety, efficiency and green transition. The examples span port risk monitoring, vessel and waterway safety, intelligent scheduling, logistics coordination, shipping-cost analysis and carbon management. The document records ministry policy direction, not completed deployment. It provides no funding or deadlines and reports no measured changes in safety, productivity, costs or emissions.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Ministry of Transport of China issued a water-transport AI application-scenario guide dated 2026-10-08 and publicly posted 2026-10-14, listing 22 scenarios grouped into safety improvement, efficiency and quality improvement, and green transition.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The guide includes proposed uses such as port safety-risk monitoring, vessel/waterway safety, port automation, rail-water coordination, intelligent shipping operations and maritime carbon accounting. It instructs agencies and organizations to choose priorities based on their circumstances and work base.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The notice does not establish deployment status, funding, deadlines, realized safety or productivity gains, cost reductions, or emissions effects for the listed scenarios.

evidence_gaps.description: The issued guide names scenarios and asks organizations to choose priorities, but does not identify funded projects, procurement, deployment status, timelines or implementation owners for each scenario.
No measured safety, throughput, logistics cost, service reliability or emissions outcome is reported for these AI applications.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented, ministry guidance spanning port safety, waterway operations, shipping logistics and maritime carbon management could direct AI adoption in an economically significant sector. The document establishes formal direction only; implementation and effects remain unmeasured.
limitations: The first-party ministry notice establishes formal guidance and the ministry's stated priorities, not that any listed system is deployed.
No funding commitments, mandatory deadlines, procurement, adoption rates or project owners are specified in the notice reviewed.
Potential safety, productivity, cost and emissions benefits are not measured here; the scenarios span heterogeneous transport tasks and would require separate evaluations.
This review covers one national ministry document and its same-ministry interpretation, not provincial uptake or global policy coverage.
brief.summary: China's Ministry of Transport issued a Chinese-language guide identifying 22 priority AI application scenarios for water transport, grouped under safety, efficiency and green transition. The examples span port risk monitoring, vessel and waterway safety, intelligent scheduling, logistics coordination, shipping-cost analysis and carbon management. The document records ministry policy direction, not completed deployment. It provides no funding or deadlines and reports no measured changes in safety, productivity, costs or emissions.

technical.claimed_result: The Ministry lists 22 scenarios in three groups: 9 for safety, 10 for efficiency/quality and 3 for green transition.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official Chinese-language notice and its ministry interpretation are accessible and dated. They document the issuance and scenario list; no deployment or measured operational result was inspected.
technical.mechanism: The ministry turns broad AI-in-transport policy into a list of 22 water-transport application scenarios and asks relevant units to select priorities, pursue technical breakthroughs, apply results and summarize cases. The guide itself does not specify a common model architecture, procurement path or evaluation method.
technical.regime: China water transport, including port safety and operations, vessel/waterway management, logistics and shipping services, and carbon management. Policy issuance is national; implementation varies by agency and operator.
technical.strongest_baseline: The notice provides policy direction, not an empirical comparison. No pre-policy adoption baseline or post-deployment outcome data was included.

brief.title: China's transport ministry sets out 22 AI application scenarios for water transport
brief.why_it_matters: The guidance gives ports, shipping firms and public transport units a national ministry's scenario list for directing AI pilots and technical work across a strategically important logistics sector. Whether it changes procurement, adoption or operational outcomes remains unmeasured.
